items.title: CVE-2026-116672 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Directly compromises OAuth/OIDC authorization servers, enabling token interception and client takeover in core Digital Identity infrastructure.

items.title: CVE-2026-104189 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Authorization bypass in Nextcloud 3D Viewer exposes password-protected shared files, impacting secure document exchange in Government, Healthcare, and Finance sectors.

items.title: CVE-2026-111107 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Unauthenticated management-plane DoS in widely deployed enterprise firewalls, directly impacting government, healthcare, and financial network perimeters and administrative control.

items.title: CVE-2026-112352 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Critical authentication bypass in Sunhillo SureLine surveillance gateways deployed across FAA, defense, and utility networks, posing severe risks to Government and national security infrastructure.

items.title: CVE-2026-112353 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Actively exploited stored XSS in enterprise webmail enables direct credential and session theft, directly impacting Digital Identity and regulated sector communications.

items.title: CVE-2026-77167 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Persistent unauthenticated DoS on Nextcloud Server, a widely deployed digital sovereignty platform critical for government and healthcare collaboration and data availability.

items.title: CVE-2026-57190 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: SQL injection in Asterisk PBX logging backends impacts Government and enterprise telecommunications infrastructure.

items.title: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Details the underground infrastructure ecosystem enabling global phishing campaigns, highlighting shared hosting, domain generation algorithms, and proxy networks. Defenders can leverage these IOCs to block malicious infrastructure at the network perimeter and enhance DNS filtering policies.

items.title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Analyzes the EvilTokens campaign exploiting Microsoft device code authentication flows to bypass MFA. The report outlines attacker infrastructure, token theft mechanisms, and detection strategies for identity protection teams to monitor anomalous device code approvals.

items.title: AI-powered phishkit arms criminals with account-hijacking tools in 10 minutes | Malwarebytes
items.excerpt: Examines an AI-driven phishing kit that automates credential harvesting and account takeover in under ten minutes. Highlights rapid deployment capabilities, dynamic page generation, and evasion techniques. Recommends implementing adaptive MFA, user training, and behavioral analytics to mitigate automated identity theft.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Explores a campaign leveraging AI to craft highly personalized device code phishing prompts, increasing success rates against enterprise users. Provides technical breakdowns of prompt engineering, infrastructure patterns, and detection rules for SIEM and identity governance platforms.

items.title: Inside Tycoon2FA: How a leading AiTM phishing kit operated at scale | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Dissects the Tycoon2FA Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing kit, detailing its real-time session hijacking capabilities and proxy architecture. Offers actionable guidance for infrastructure teams to deploy certificate pinning, monitor for suspicious proxy traffic, and enforce phishing-resistant MFA.

items.title: Joint advisory: state-sponsored spear-phishing campaigns targeting critical infrastructure - SUVAT
items.excerpt: Covers coordinated state-sponsored spear-phishing operations targeting critical infrastructure sectors. Details TTPs, malicious attachments, and initial access vectors. Advises defenders to harden email gateways, segment OT/IT networks, and monitor for lateral movement indicators.

items.title: Foreign Threat Actor Conducting Large-Scale Spearphishing Campaign with RDP Attachments | CISA
items.excerpt: Alerts on large-scale spear-phishing campaigns distributing malicious RDP files to compromise remote access infrastructure. Provides mitigation steps including disabling RDP where unnecessary, enforcing network-level authentication, and monitoring for unauthorized remote connections.

items.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts large-scale spear-phishing campaign using RDP files | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Analyzes a state-sponsored campaign using spear-phished RDP files to gain initial access to government and enterprise networks. Highlights persistence mechanisms, credential dumping techniques, and defensive strategies for securing remote access and identity management systems.

items.title: CVE-2026-94380
items.excerpt:
Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password vulnerability in HAVELSAN Inc. Liman MYS allows Password Recovery Exploitation.

This issue affects Liman MYS: from 2.3.4-1124 before 2.3.5-1131.

items.title: CVE-2026-101034
items.excerpt: An attacker who obtained the hardcoded key could decrypt domain/service account passwords, task run-as credentials, and sysprep passwords stored in or transmitted by GSS Deployment Server installation.

items.title: CVE-2026-89209
items.excerpt: A vulnerability has been identified in Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible) (All versions < V4.2.4), Mendix SAML (Mendix 11 compatible) (All versions < V4.2.4), Mendix SAML (Mendix 9 compatible) (All versions < V3.6.29). Affected versions of the module do not properly protect against SAML assertion replay in IdP-initiated authentication flows. This could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the application by replaying a valid SAML response.
